9. COMBINED HORMONAL CONTRACEPTION

✓1/3’d UK women aged 16—44 years had used oral contraception
✓CHC -estrogen and a progestogen
•A pill (COC)
•Transdermal Patch CTP
•Vaginal ring CVR

PERFECT USE VS TYPICAL USE

Many contraceptive methods are affected by human error such as forgetting to take your pill. They may be very effective with "perfect use" but the effectiveness of certain methods as "typically used" is likely to be lower.

Perfect use: of a contraceptive method is when it is used correctly all the time.

Typical use: is what generally happens in real life. It takes into account human error.

✓ Effectiveness could also be affected by drug interactions (all CHC methods) and malabsorption (COC only). CONTRACEPTIVE EFFECTIVENESS:

CHC is highly user-dependent:

•VTE: CHC is associated with increased risk of VTE;
•dependent on progestogen type and estrogen dose

•Breast cancer: small increased risk of breast cancer which reduces with time after stopping CHC.
•Cervical cancer: current use of CHC for > 5 years has a small increased risk of cervical cancer risk reduces over time after stopping CHC and is no longer increased by about 10 years after stopping.

Hormone free interval HFI can be associated with these defects including mood chance headache and unscheduled bleeding.

Concomitant use of other drugs:

•Hepatic enzyme-inducing drugs could reduce the contraceptive effectiveness of all CHC methods. It can affect serum levels of drugs such as lamotrigine with potential significant clinical effects

Choice of contraceptive method:

•A COC containing < 30 ug EE in combination with LNG or NET is a reasonable first-line option to minimize (VTE) risk.

CHC, formulation and regimen:

•Estrogens: In the UK, the majority of COC as well as the CTP and CVR, contain between 20 µg and 35 µg of the synthetic estrogen, EE.
•Progestogens:
⮤First: norethisterone (NET)
⮤Second: levonorgestrel (LNG)
⮤Third: Desogestrel, gestagens, norgestimate

Newer/Formulations:

⇨Co-cyprindiol (containing 35 µg EE with cyproterone acetate, an anti-androgen) is indicated for management of moderate to severe acne and hirsutism. Women using co-cyprindiol for these indications do not require additional contraception.

Studies revealed that suppression of ovarian activity with low-dose COCs with 7-day HFIs is suboptimal. Loss of ovarian suppression during 7-day HFIs is commonly associated with follicular development, and

⇨most dominant follicles appear during this period. By contrast, increased ovarian suppression was noted in regimens that shortened or eliminated the HFI, or that substituted low-dose ethinyl estradiol for the HFI.
⇨Extended regimens with modified HFIs may provide greater ovarian suppression with the potential for increased contraceptive effectiveness.

Non-contraceptive health benefits:

✓Reduce HMB
✓menstrual pain
✓improve acne.
✓Premenstrual syndrome symptoms.
✓Reduce risk of recurrence of endometriosis after surgical management.
✓CHC can be used for management of pcos.
✓Significant reduction in risk of endometrial and ovarian cancer that increases with duration of chc use and persists for many years after stopping chc
✓Reduced risk of colorectal cancer

Women using combined hormonal contraception: key indications for medical review

Key symptoms that should prompt women to seek urgent medical review

⮤Calf pain, swelling and/or redness
⮤Chest pain and/or breathlessness and/or coughing up blood
⮤Loss of motor or sensory function

Key symptoms that should prompt women to seek medical review

⮤Breast lump, unilateral nipple discharge, new nipple inversion, change in breast skin
⮤New onset migraine
⮤New onset sensory or motor symptoms in the hour preceding onset of migraine
⮤Persistent unscheduled vaginal bleeding

New medical diagnoses that should prompt women to seek advice from their contraceptive provider (and review of the suitability of CHC)

⮤High blood pressure
⮤High body mass index (>35 kg/m²)
⮤Migraine or migraine with aura
⮤Deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism
⮤Blood clotting abnormality
⮤Antiphospholipid antibodies
⮤Angina, heart attack, stroke or peripheral vascular disease
⮤Atrial fibrillation
⮤Cardiomyopathy
⮤Breast cancer or breast cancer gene mutation
⮤Liver tumor
⮤Symptomatic gallstones
